reader.requirement: The compiler must refuse a CONTROL clause in which two recurrences of data-name-1 (each possibly qualified) identify the same data item, judged by the item identified (a level 66 without THROUGH identifies the item it renames), and accept recurrences that identify different items: same name in different groups, a group and its subordinate, a REDEFINES item, a level 66 with THROUGH.

the §2023:13.18.16.3 SR6 written-reference uniqueness screen runs only at DialectLevel >= 2002
a reference-modified CONTROL operand requires COBOL-2002 (COBOL0900 at 85), so the refmod exemption in ScreenControlItemsDistinct is unreachable at 85

reader.notes: The 85 arm compares resolved items (AttributeItem), so spelling differences and a 66 without THROUGH are caught and distinct items pass; the 2023 written-reference screen is switched off at 85. The edition gate refuses reference modification at 85 before the item screen could exempt it.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:XIII.3.7.2-3.7.3, §1985:VI.5.11 (RENAMES) and §1985:IV.4.3.2.1, and ReportSectionBinder.cs#ScreenControlItemsDistinct (85 arm compares AttributeItem). Probes at --std 85: c1 (G1 with S/B and A; 66 R1 RENAMES A; 66 R2 RENAMES A; CONTROLS R1 R2 B OF G1 B OF S OF G1) -> COBOL1699 'R2' identifies the data item 'A' that 'R1' already identifies, and COBOL1699 'B OF S OF G1' identifies 'B' that 'B OF G1' already identifies (a COBOL2692 from my own name clash of R1 with the report-name is incidental); c3 (CONTROL IS A in one RD and FINAL A G2 RT in another, 66 RT RENAMES A THRU C occupying exactly G2's characters) -> compiles and runs, control footing on the break, 'DONE'. The identical-item and spelled-twice halves are decided and correct. THE DOUBT: every refusal of a level-66 entry without THROUGH (reader ctl7, my c1 R1/R2) rests on reading 'identify a different data item' so that such a 66 entry IS the item it renames. The 1985 text does not say that: GR2 transfers 'all of the data attributes of data-name-2' to data-name-1 (it does not equate them), §1985:IV.4.3.2.1 counts a 66 entry among 'Entries that specify elementary items or groups introduced by a RENAMES clause' (the entry specifies its own item), and §1985:VI.5.11.1 calls RENAMES 'alternative, possibly overlapping, groupings'. The compiler treats as DIFFERENT items a REDEFINES item (ctl5) and a 66 THRU entry covering exactly another group's characters (c3, RT beside G2), yet as the SAME item a 66 entry without THRU: the line is drawn by the reading, not by the text. Under the other reading CONTROLS SG RG (RG RENAMES SG) and CONTROLS R1 R2 are legal and the compiler rejects legal source. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR2  (3.7.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:VI.5.11.4 GR2  (5.11.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:VI.5.11.1  (5.11.1 Function)  the text is in the clause'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.2.1  (4.3.2.1 Level-Numbers)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GR1'.
refuter.corrected: CONFORMS on the reading that a level-66 entry without THROUGH identifies the item it renames (GR2); that reading needs an adjudication recorded in docs/conformance/ (a one-file entry) before the verdict closes, since the alternative reading (a 66 entry specifies its own data item, §1985:IV.4.3.2.1) makes the ctl7 and c1 refusals rejects-legal-source.

adjudication.reason: The doubt is rejected: a level-66 entry without THROUGH takes all of the data attributes of the item it renames (§1985:VI.5.11.4 GR2) and has no description of its own, so it identifies that item; a REDEFINES item and a level-66 entry WITH THROUGH (a group of its own, GR1) identify different items. The reading is kb/Work PB5866's (landed). GnuCOBOL 3.2.0 has no check of the rule and settles nothing.
